name: Nirvana
hook: A trio from a depressed logging town whose second album accidentally ended hair metal's run on American radio.

blurb.age7: Nirvana was a rock band whose loud, angry song 'Smells Like Teen Spirit' became huge in 1991 and changed what was popular on the radio.
blurb.age13: Kurt Cobain, Krist Novoselic, and eventually drummer Dave Grohl formed Nirvana in Aberdeen, Washington, a struggling logging town. Their 1991 album 'Nevermind', led by 'Smells Like Teen Spirit', became an unexpected massive hit and pushed the polished hair metal that had dominated American rock radio out of fashion almost overnight. Cobain died by suicide in 1994.
blurb.adult: Nirvana's commercial breakthrough is one of the clearest documented pivot points in American rock radio: 'Nevermind' displaced Michael Jackson's 'Dangerous' at number one in January 1992, and the shift toward the quieter-verse-loud-chorus dynamic Cobain borrowed from underground bands like the Pixies reshaped mainstream rock programming for years afterward. Cobain's 1994 suicide, following years of heroin addiction, is part of the story of how quickly the band's success turned difficult for him personally.

signatureTracks.title: Smells Like Teen Spirit
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The single that broke the album and, with it, mainstream rock radio's format almost overnight.

signatureTracks.title: The Man Who Sold the World
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Their MTV Unplugged cover of David Bowie's 1970 song, recorded months before Cobain's death.
